gen-fs-styro-gf-athiti: Retro and commanding, Styro crowds its letters until they nearly touch. Athiti, a sans-serif, keeps each s see-through and its strokes a single line width, so extended reading moves along without a snag.
gen-fs-styro-gf-biryani: Tight, crowded retro letters give Styro a stamped-down, commanding look. Biryani leaves every small counter unclogged and bends its curves like cord, a loosening that is this pair's best trick.
gen-fs-styro-gf-funnel-sans: Crowded, close-set letters give Styro its retro punch. Funnel Sans, a sans-serif with almost no stroke contrast, keeps its e pried open and its lines steady across a full page.
gen-fs-styro-gf-martel-sans: Styro hits hard: retro, commanding, letters packed nearly shoulder to shoulder. Martel Sans, a modern sans with generous curve openings and a high mean line, supplies the pair's single best quality: relief.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-mono: Styro lands with a retro thump, its letters crowded and commanding. Noto Sans Mono steps in with spaced-out, tall, sturdy sans letters, loosening everything the heading squeezes together.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-ol-chiki: Styro is a retro thump, its crowded, commanding letters pressed nearly shut with barely any gap showing. Noto Sans Ol Chiki pulls its curve tails back, forming solid blocks.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-old-italic: Noto Sans Old Italic barely separates small letters from capitals. Styro does the loud, retro, commanding work up top, while the body font keeps its curve endings well apart for quiet legibility.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-old-persian: Styro is retro and commanding, its letters jammed nearly shut. Noto Sans Old Persian, lofty and open, lets text breathe into the white space, so extended reading feels light.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-oriya: Approachable Noto Sans Oriya sits against crowded, commanding Styro. Its curve gaps stay generous and its small letters rise almost to cap height, so paragraphs of sans text move along easily.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-osage: Squeezed, retro and commanding, Styro packs its letters tight. Noto Sans Osage, a sans-serif of inflated lowercase bowls and sweeping curves, fills the line generously beneath that tight squeeze.
